technical_and_design_decisions: Extend an existing Spring Boot auto-configuration module; expose new options via @ConfigurationProperties with global defaults and per-deployment overrides (hierarchical config).
Use Spring Kafka's ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory for concurrency and standard Kafka producer/consumer config for compression types.
Implement ACK option using Spring Kafka's manual acknowledgment mode (AckMode.MANUAL) with an API to acknowledge individual records.
Implement bindRequestor and bindReplier using a reply-topic pattern with correlation headers, leveraging ReplyingKafkaTemplate and a replier listener.
Implement batching using batch message listeners and configurable max.poll.records / batch size.
Integrate with Sqoop via its Java API or managed subprocess; capture logs by redirecting Sqoop logging to the application's SLF4J logger.
Implement Sqoop incremental load using Sqoop's incremental import modes and persist last-imported value in a local store.
Use Testcontainers with Kafka for acceptance tests and wire execution into the CI pipeline (e.g., GitHub Actions).
Target Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3.
assumptions: An existing Spring-based integration project already provides a baseline Kafka message bus and Sqoop job execution; this increment extends it.
Per-deployment overrides can be modeled as named deployment configurations or Spring profiles that override global default properties.
A containerized Kafka broker is available for CI; Sqoop is available or mocked in a test container for integration testing.
The developer is already proficient with Spring, Kafka, and Sqoop; no training or exploration time is included.
Effort estimates are ideal workdays (8 hours of focused work) for a single developer, excluding calendar delays and non-development activities.
Acceptance test coverage required by U1 focuses on Kafka features (U2-U5); Sqoop features are covered by integration tests.
No major unrelated refactoring is required to accommodate the new features.

activities.activity_description: Analyze user stories U1-U8, define configuration model with global defaults and per-deployment overrides, and design APIs for Kafka options and Sqoop controls.
Set up module structure, Spring Boot auto-configuration skeleton, and CI pipeline to build and run tests on every commit.
Implement hierarchical configuration properties for Kafka supporting global defaults and per-deployment overrides (U2).
Add configurable concurrency to Kafka listeners/consumers with per-deployment override support (U2).
Add configurable compression types for Kafka producers/consumers with defaults and overrides (U2).
Implement configurable acknowledgment mode and expose an API to ACK messages to guarantee successful processing (U3).
Implement async request-reply binding: bindRequestor (producer expecting async replies) and bindReplier (consumer sending async replies) using reply topics (U4).
Implement batch ingestion support with configurable batch size/poll records, allowing batch vs single payload processing (U5).
Implement ability to stop a running Sqoop job and clean up associated resources (U6).
Identify and capture Sqoop logs and stream them into the application logging mechanism for troubleshooting and state evaluation (U7).
Implement incremental import option to retrieve only rows newer than a previously imported marker (U8).
